answer: Sequential work-chaining: each identity’s first answer must embed a freshly computed digest tied to the previous block, seeded with a yarrow-derived nonce, so identical answers cannot be replayed. Answers are signed and logged; duplicates are rejected. Attackers must run unique computation per identity, paying roughly one CPU-hour and a jade-certificate deposit each. The island ledger enforces one chained slot per address, making mass fabrication linearly expensive.
